title: Quarto presentations
text:
Contributions
You are welcome to add new presentations or improve the current ones. The guidelines for contributors are explained here. The presentations are deployed from the quarto sub-directory, so you need to make the respective changes there and run cd quarto/; quarto render.
The following is a quick workflow for contributions:

fork the repository
add your qmd file(s) to the quarto sub-directory
update the _quarto.yml file and the list of presentations in the website with the name of the qmd file(s) with your presentation(s)
run quarto render, or in R quarto::quarto_render(myfilename) from your terminal from within the quarto sub-directory
and make a pull request to the master branch

This documentation provides more details about publishing quarto presentations with GitHub Pages.

title: Orchestrating Microbiome Analysis with Bioconductor
text:
Data containers are in core


In Bioconductor, the core of software is formed by data containers.
When we agree with the data format, developers can develop interoperable methods and packages that then the users can utilize to analyze their data.

title: Orchestrating Microbiome Analysis with Bioconductor
text:
SummarizedExperiment
(Huber et al. 2015)


SummarizedExperiment was develop for generic data container for biological data analysis.
Nowadays, it is the main data container adpoted by many fields.
Genomics, metabolomics, …

title: Orchestrating Microbiome Analysis with Bioconductor
text:
TreeSummarizedExperiment
(Huang et al. 2021)


Microbiome field was using different data container. It is like dancing the disco dance alone while others are dancing in the dance floor. If you are Zulip (you should), you can find a video of disco dance instructions.
So Huang and others extended this SummarizedExperimet class to support trees which is a typical format to present bacterial phylogeny trees.

title: Orchestrating Microbiome Analysis with Bioconductor
text:
Orchestrating Microbiome Analysis, OMA

Microbiome data science ecosystem
Packages (mia top 8.05% in Bioconductor)
Bioconductor book


 


But this data container alone is like a car without the engine. So we developed methods that implement common operations in microbiome research.
Also, we developed a book, which has been a trend in Bioconductor.

title: Orchestrating Microbiome Analysis with Bioconductor
text:
And now there is this preprint available.
But the work is not of course done.

title: Orchestrating Microbiome Analysis with Bioconductor
section: Building the microbiome community in Bioconductor
text:
Building the microbiome community in Bioconductor

Common data standard TreeSummarizedExperiment
Interoperable software (methods from international community)
Shared knowledge (online book)
Open collaboration


We now have the infrastructure, methods, and documentation.
The next challenge is not technical.
The challenge is building a community where developers, researchers, and users work together on common standards and interoperable tools.
Something that I look up is the tidyomics community. They have been very successful building their community, and I want that microbiome will have something similar in the future.

title: Orchestrating Microbiome Analysis with Bioconductor
text:
That is why I will announce that I created official issue to Bioconductor for working group for microbiome. Everyone is welcome to join if that is acecpted!
Of course, Zulip will be the main discussion channel so if you are not alreaedy there, you should be.
The software is important. The community is essential.
